entries.title: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual: Oral Cavity Carcinoma (8th Edition)
key_innovations: Incorporation of Depth of Invasion (DOI) into T category
Incorporation of Extranodal Extension (ENE) into N category (clinical ENEc and pathological ENEp)

t_definitions.T1: Tumor <= 2 cm in greatest dimension and <= 5 mm depth of invasion (DOI)
t_definitions.T2: Tumor <= 2 cm with DOI > 5 mm and <= 10 mm; OR tumor > 2 cm and <= 4 cm with DOI <= 10 mm
t_definitions.T3: Tumor > 4 cm in greatest dimension OR any tumor with DOI > 10 mm and <= 20 mm
t_definitions.T4a: Moderately advanced local disease: tumor invades adjacent structures (cortical bone of mandible or maxilla, maxillary sinus, skin of face) OR DOI > 20 mm
t_definitions.T4b: Very advanced local disease: tumor invades masticator space, pterygoid plates, or skull base, and/or encases internal carotid artery

n_definitions_clinical.NX: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed
n_definitions_clinical.N1: Metastasis in a single ipsilateral lymph node, <= 3 cm in greatest dimension, ENE(-)
n_definitions_clinical.N2a: Metastasis in a single ipsilateral lymph node, > 3 cm but <= 6 cm, ENE(-)
n_definitions_clinical.N2b: Metastasis in multiple ipsilateral lymph nodes, none > 6 cm, ENE(-)
n_definitions_clinical.N2c: Metastasis in bilateral or contralateral lymph nodes, none > 6 cm, ENE(-)
n_definitions_clinical.N3a: Metastasis in a lymph node > 6 cm in greatest dimension, ENE(-)
n_definitions_clinical.N3b: Metastasis in any lymph node(s) with clinically overt extranodal extension (ENE(+))

key_passages.text: Depth of invasion (DOI) is measured from the reconstructed mucosal basement membrane line to the deepest point of tumor invasion. It is distinct from total tumor thickness.
Clinical ENE is defined by evidence of skin involvement, soft tissue fixation, or nerve invasion matching the location of regional lymph nodes.

entries.title: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual: HPV-Mediated (p16-Positive) Oropharyngeal Cancer
key_innovations: Separate staging system for p16-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma
Dramatic stage down-classification reflecting superior overall survival with definitive chemoradiation
Clinical N (cN) distinct from pathological N (pN); ENE is omitted from HPV-positive N staging

t_definitions.T0: No primary tumor identified (e.g. occult primary presenting with p16+ nodal metastasis)
t_definitions.T2: Tumor > 2 cm but <= 4 cm in greatest dimension
t_definitions.T3: Tumor > 4 cm in greatest dimension or extension to lingual surface of epiglottis
t_definitions.T4: Moderately advanced local disease: tumor invades larynx, deep/extrinsic muscle of tongue, medial pterygoid, hard palate, or mandible or beyond

n_definitions_clinical.cN1: One or more ipsilateral lymph nodes, none > 6 cm in greatest dimension
n_definitions_clinical.cN2: Contralateral or bilateral lymph nodes, none > 6 cm in greatest dimension
n_definitions_clinical.cN3: Lymph node(s) > 6 cm in greatest dimension

n_definitions_pathological.pN2: Metastasis in 5 or more lymph nodes

clinical_stage_groups.Stage II: T0-T2, cN2, M0 OR T3, cN0-cN2, M0
clinical_stage_groups.Stage III: T4, any cN, M0 OR any T, cN3, M0

key_passages.text: Staging under this chapter requires confirmed p16 overexpression (>= 70% strong diffuse nuclear and cytoplasmic staining). Non-HPV/p16-negative oropharyngeal tumors must be staged under the conventional H&N staging system.

entries.title: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma

t_definitions.T1: Tumor confined to nasopharynx, or extends to oropharynx and/or nasal cavity without parapharyngeal involvement
t_definitions.T2: Tumor with extension to parapharyngeal space and/or infiltration of medial pterygoid, lateral pterygoid, and/or prevertebral muscles
t_definitions.T3: Tumor invades bony structures of skull base, cervical vertebra, pterygoid structures, and/or paranasal sinuses
t_definitions.T4: Tumor with intracranial extension, involvement of cranial nerves, hypopharynx, orbit, parotid gland, and/or extensive soft tissue infiltration beyond the lateral surface of the lateral pterygoid muscle

n_definitions.N1: Unilateral cervical lymph node(s) and/or unilateral or bilateral retropharyngeal lymph nodes, <= 6 cm, above the caudal border of the cricoid cartilage
n_definitions.N2: Bilateral cervical lymph node(s), <= 6 cm, above the caudal border of the cricoid cartilage
n_definitions.N3: Cervical lymph node(s) > 6 cm in greatest dimension and/or extension below the caudal border of the cricoid cartilage

stage_groups.Stage II: T1 N1 M0, T2 N0-N1 M0
stage_groups.Stage III: T1-T2 N2 M0, T3 N0-N2 M0
stage_groups.Stage IVA: T4 any N M0, or any T N3 M0

entries.title: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual: Larynx (Glottis and Supraglottis)

glottic_t_definitions.T1: Tumor limited to vocal cord(s) (may involve anterior or posterior commissure) with normal mobility; T1a: one vocal cord; T1b: both vocal cords
glottic_t_definitions.T2: Tumor extends to supraglottis and/or subglottis, and/or with impaired vocal cord mobility
glottic_t_definitions.T3: Tumor limited to larynx with vocal cord fixation and/or invasion of paraglottic space and/or inner cortex of thyroid cartilage
glottic_t_definitions.T4a: Moderately advanced local disease: tumor invades through the thyroid cartilage and/or invades tissues beyond larynx (trachea, soft tissues of neck including deep extrinsic muscle of tongue, strap muscles, thyroid, or esophagus)
glottic_t_definitions.T4b: Very advanced local disease: tumor invades prevertebral space, encases carotid artery, or invades mediastinal structures

supraglottic_t_definitions.T1: Tumor limited to one subsite of supraglottis with normal vocal cord mobility
supraglottic_t_definitions.T2: Tumor invades mucosa of more than one adjacent subsite of supraglottis or glottis or region outside the supraglottis without fixation of the larynx
supraglottic_t_definitions.T3: Tumor limited to larynx with vocal cord fixation and/or invades any of: paraglottic space, pre-epiglottic space, inner cortex of thyroid cartilage
supraglottic_t_definitions.T4a: Invades through thyroid cartilage and/or extends into tissues beyond larynx
supraglottic_t_definitions.T4b: Invades prevertebral space, encases carotid artery, or invades mediastinal structures

entries.title: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual / IASLC 8th & 9th Editions: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
entries.organization: AJCC / International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC)

t_definitions.T1mi: Minimally invasive adenocarcinoma (<= 3 cm solitary, <= 5 mm invasive component)
t_definitions.T1b: Tumor > 1 cm but <= 2 cm in greatest dimension
t_definitions.T1c: Tumor > 2 cm but <= 3 cm in greatest dimension
t_definitions.T2a: Tumor > 3 cm but <= 4 cm; OR involves main bronchus without carina, invades visceral pleura, atelectasis/obstructive pneumonitis extending to hilum
t_definitions.T2b: Tumor > 4 cm but <= 5 cm in greatest dimension
t_definitions.T3: Tumor > 5 cm but <= 7 cm; OR separate tumor nodule(s) in the same lobe; OR directly invades parietal pleura, chest wall, phrenic nerve, parietal pericardium
t_definitions.T4: Tumor > 7 cm; OR separate tumor nodule(s) in a different ipsilateral lobe; OR invades diaphragm, mediastinum, heart, great vessels, trachea, recurrent laryngeal nerve, esophagus, vertebral body, carina

n_definitions.N1: Metastasis in ipsilateral peribronchial, hilar, or intrapulmonary nodes (stations 10-14)
n_definitions.N2: Metastasis in ipsilateral mediastinal and/or subcarinal lymph nodes (stations 2, 4, 7). IASLC 9th subcategorizes into N2a (single station) and N2b (multiple stations)
n_definitions.N3: Metastasis in contralateral mediastinal, contralateral hilar, or scalene/supraclavicular lymph nodes (stations 1, etc.)

m_definitions.M1a: Malignant pleural/pericardial effusion, pleural/pericardial nodules, or separate nodule in contralateral lobe
m_definitions.M1b: Single extrathoracic metastasis in a single organ
m_definitions.M1c: Multiple extrathoracic metastases in one or multiple organs. IASLC 9th: M1c1 (single organ multiple lesions), M1c2 (multiple organs)

stage_groups.Stage IIB: T1a-c N1 M0, T2a-b N1 M0, T3 N0 M0
stage_groups.Stage IIIA: T1a-c N2 M0, T2a-b N2 M0, T3 N1 M0, T4 N0-N1 M0
stage_groups.Stage IIIB: T1a-c N3 M0, T2a-b N3 M0, T3 N2 M0, T4 N2 M0
stage_groups.Stage IIIC: T3 N3 M0, T4 N3 M0

entries.title: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual: Breast Cancer (Anatomic & Prognostic Staging)
key_innovations: Integration of Anatomic Stage (T, N, M) and Clinical/Pathological Prognostic Stage (incorporating ER, PR, HER2, Grade, and Oncotype DX)

t_definitions.Tis: Carcinoma in situ (DCIS, LCIS removed as non-malignant, Paget disease of nipple with no tumor)
t_definitions.T4a: Extension to chest wall (not including pectoralis muscle alone)
t_definitions.T4b: Ulceration and/or ipsilateral satellite skin nodules and/or edema (including peau d'orange)

n_definitions_clinical.cN1: Metastases to movable ipsilateral level I, II axillary lymph node(s)
n_definitions_clinical.cN2a: Metastases in ipsilateral level I, II axillary lymph nodes fixed to one another or other structures
n_definitions_clinical.cN2b: Metastases in clinically detected ipsilateral internal mammary nodes with negative axillary nodes
n_definitions_clinical.cN3a: Metastases in ipsilateral infraclavicular (level III axillary) lymph node(s)
n_definitions_clinical.cN3b: Metastases in ipsilateral internal mammary and axillary lymph nodes
n_definitions_clinical.cN3c: Metastases in ipsilateral supraclavicular lymph node(s)

n_definitions_pathological.pN0: No regional lymph node metastasis histologically (pN0(i+) if isolated tumor clusters <= 0.2 mm or < 200 cells)
n_definitions_pathological.pN1mi: Micrometastases (> 0.2 mm to <= 2.0 mm and/or > 200 cells)
n_definitions_pathological.pN1a: Metastases in 1-3 axillary lymph nodes, at least one > 2.0 mm
n_definitions_pathological.pN1b: Internal mammary nodes with micrometastases or macrometastases detected by SLN biopsy
n_definitions_pathological.pN2b: Metastases in clinically detected internal mammary lymph nodes in the absence of axillary lymph node metastases
n_definitions_pathological.pN3a: Metastases in 10 or more axillary lymph nodes, or in infraclavicular (level III) lymph nodes
n_definitions_pathological.pN3b: Metastases in clinically detected internal mammary nodes with positive axillary nodes, or > 3 axillary nodes with microscopic IMN
n_definitions_pathological.pN3c: Metastases in ipsilateral supraclavicular lymph nodes

entries.title: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual: Prostate Cancer (8th Edition)

clinical_t_definitions.cT1: Clinically inapparent tumor not palpable (cT1a <= 5% resected, cT1b > 5% resected, cT1c needle biopsy identified)
clinical_t_definitions.cT2: Palpable tumor confined within prostate (cT2a <= 1/2 of one side, cT2b > 1/2 of one side, cT2c bilateral)
clinical_t_definitions.cT3: Extraprostatic extension (cT3a EPE unilateral/bilateral or bladder neck microscopic invasion, cT3b seminal vesicle invasion)
clinical_t_definitions.cT4: Tumor fixed or invades adjacent structures other than seminal vesicles: external sphincter, rectum, bladder, levators, pelvic wall

pathological_t_definitions.pT2: Organ-confined prostate cancer (subcategories pT2a/b/c eliminated in 8th edition)
pathological_t_definitions.pT3a: Extraprostatic extension (unilateral or bilateral) or microscopic invasion of bladder neck
pathological_t_definitions.pT4: Direct invasion of adjacent organs (bladder, rectum, external sphincter, levator muscles, and/or pelvic wall)

n_definitions.N0: No positive regional nodes (pelvic: internal iliac, external iliac, obturator, presacral)

m_definitions.M1b: Bone metastasis (with or without other non-visceral metastases)
m_definitions.M1c: Other distant site(s) with or without bone disease

prognostic_stage_groups.Stage I: cT1-2a, N0, M0, PSA < 10, Grade Group 1
prognostic_stage_groups.Stage IIA: cT1-cT2a, N0, M0, PSA 10 to < 20, Grade Group 1; OR cT2b-c, N0, M0, PSA < 20, Grade Group 1
prognostic_stage_groups.Stage IIB: cT1-cT2, N0, M0, PSA < 20, Grade Group 2
prognostic_stage_groups.Stage IIC: cT1-cT2, N0, M0, PSA < 20, Grade Group 3 or 4
prognostic_stage_groups.Stage IIIA: cT1-cT2, N0, M0, PSA >= 20, Grade Group 1-4
prognostic_stage_groups.Stage IIIB: cT3-cT4, N0, M0, any PSA, Grade Group 1-4
prognostic_stage_groups.Stage IIIC: Any cT, N0, M0, any PSA, Grade Group 5
prognostic_stage_groups.Stage IV: Any cT, N1, M0 OR Any cT, any N, M1

entries.title: FIGO 2018 / AJCC 9th Edition Cervical Cancer Staging Classification
entries.organization: International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) / AJCC
key_innovations: Allows clinical, radiological (r), and pathological (p) findings for stage assignment
Stage IIIC added for regional nodal involvement: IIIC1 (pelvic) vs IIIC2 (para-aortic)
Stage IB divided into IB1 (<= 2 cm), IB2 (> 2 to 4 cm), and IB3 (> 4 cm)

t_definitions.T1 / Stage I: Cervical carcinoma confined to uterus (corpus extension disregarded)
t_definitions.T1a1 / IA1: Measured stromal invasion <= 3.0 mm in depth
t_definitions.T1a2 / IA2: Measured stromal invasion > 3.0 mm and <= 5.0 mm in depth
t_definitions.T1b1 / IB1: Invasive carcinoma >= 5.0 mm depth of invasion and <= 2.0 cm in greatest dimension
t_definitions.T1b2 / IB2: Invasive carcinoma > 2.0 cm and <= 4.0 cm in greatest dimension
t_definitions.T1b3 / IB3: Invasive carcinoma > 4.0 cm in greatest dimension (formerly Stage IIA2 in FIGO 2014)
t_definitions.T2a1 / IIA1: Involvement of upper 2/3 of vagina without parametrial invasion, <= 4.0 cm
t_definitions.T2a2 / IIA2: Involvement of upper 2/3 of vagina without parametrial invasion, > 4.0 cm
t_definitions.T2b / IIB: Carcinoma with parametrial invasion, not extending to pelvic sidewall
t_definitions.T3a / IIIA: Carcinoma involves lower third of vagina, with no extension to pelvic sidewall
t_definitions.T3b / IIIB: Extension to pelvic sidewall and/or causes hydronephrosis or non-functioning kidney
t_definitions.Stage IIIC1: Pelvic lymph node metastasis (IIIC1r imaging, IIIC1p pathology)
t_definitions.Stage IIIC2: Para-aortic lymph node metastasis (IIIC2r imaging, IIIC2p pathology)
t_definitions.T4 / Stage IVA: Invasion of mucosa of bladder or rectum, or extends beyond true pelvis
t_definitions.Stage IVB: Distant metastasis (including non-regional nodes, lung, liver, bone)

entries.title: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual: Colon and Rectum (8th Edition)

t_definitions.Tis: Carcinoma in situ: intramucosal carcinoma (involvement of lamina propria with no extension through muscularis mucosae)
t_definitions.T3: Tumor invades through muscularis propria into pericolorectal tissues
t_definitions.T4b: Tumor directly invades or is adherent to other organs or structures

n_definitions.N1c: Tumor deposit(s) in subserosa, mesentery, or nonperitonealized pericolic/perirectal tissues without regional nodal metastasis
n_definitions.N2b: Metastasis in 7 or more regional lymph nodes

m_definitions.M1a: Metastasis to a single site or organ without peritoneal metastasis
m_definitions.M1b: Metastasis to two or more sites or organs without peritoneal metastasis
m_definitions.M1c: Metastasis to peritoneal surface alone or with other site/organ metastases

key_passages.text: For rectal cancer, pelvic MRI must report distance of tumor or lymph node to the mesorectal fascia (CRM positive if <= 1.0 mm) and extramural vascular invasion (mrEMVI), which dictate neoadjuvant chemoradiation or Total Neoadjuvant Therapy (TNT).

entries.title: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual: Esophagus and Esophagogastric Junction
key_innovations: Separate clinical (cTNM), pathological (pTNM), and post-neoadjuvant pathological (ypTNM) stage classifications
Distinct stage groupings for Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) vs Adenocarcinoma

t_definitions.T1a: Invades lamina propria or muscularis mucosae
t_definitions.T4a: Resectable invasion of pleura, pericardium, azygos vein, diaphragm, or peritoneum
t_definitions.T4b: Unresectable invasion of aorta, vertebral body, or trachea

n_definitions.N3: Metastasis in 7 or more regional lymph nodes

entries.title: Delineation of the Neck Node Levels for Head and Neck Tumors: A 2013 Update Consensus Guidelines
entries.organization: DAHANCA, EORTC, HKNPCSG, NCIC CTG, NCRI, RTOG, TROG

Level Ia (Submental).posterior: Body of hyoid bone / mylohyoid muscle
Level Ia (Submental).lateral: Medial edge of anterior belly of digastric muscle (bilateral)
Level Ia (Submental).drainage: Floor of mouth, anterior oral tongue, anterior mandibular alveolar ridge, lower lip

Level Ib (Submandibular).cranial: Cranial edge of submandibular gland / mylohyoid muscle
Level Ib (Submandibular).caudal: Plane through caudal edge of hyoid bone and caudal edge of mandible
Level Ib (Submandibular).anterior: Symphysis menti / anterior belly of digastric muscle
Level Ib (Submandibular).posterior: Posterior edge of submandibular gland / posterior belly of digastric muscle
Level Ib (Submandibular).lateral: Inner side of mandible / platysma muscle
Level Ib (Submandibular).medial: Lateral edge of anterior belly of digastric / mylohyoid / hyoglossus
Level Ib (Submandibular).drainage: Oral cavity, anterior nasal cavity, mid-face soft tissues, submandibular gland

Level II (Upper Jugular).subdivisions: IIa (anterior to posterior border of IJV) and IIb (posterior to posterior border of IJV)
Level II (Upper Jugular).cranial: Caudal edge of lateral process of C1 (atlas)
Level II (Upper Jugular).caudal: Caudal edge of body of hyoid bone
Level II (Upper Jugular).anterior: Posterior edge of submandibular gland / posterior belly of digastric muscle
Level II (Upper Jugular).medial: Medial edge of internal carotid artery / scalene muscles
Level II (Upper Jugular).drainage: Nasal cavity, oral cavity, nasopharynx, oropharynx, hypopharynx, larynx, parotid gland

Level III (Middle Jugular).cranial: Caudal edge of body of hyoid bone
Level III (Middle Jugular).anterior: Anterior edge of SCM / posterior third of thyrohyoid muscle
Level III (Middle Jugular).medial: Medial edge of common carotid artery / scalene muscles
Level III (Middle Jugular).drainage: Base of tongue, tonsils, larynx, hypopharynx, thyroid gland

Level IVa (Lower Jugular).caudal: 2 cm cranial to sternal manubrium / sternoclavicular joint
Level IVa (Lower Jugular).anterior: Anterior edge of SCM (cranially) / body of SCM (caudally)
Level IVa (Lower Jugular).posterior: Posterior edge of SCM (cranially) / scalene muscles (caudally)
Level IVa (Lower Jugular).lateral: Deep surface of SCM (cranially) / lateral edge of SCM (caudally)
Level IVa (Lower Jugular).medial: Medial edge of common carotid artery / lateral edge of thyroid gland / scalene muscles

Level IVb (Medial Supraclavicular).cranial: Caudal border of level IVa (2 cm cranial to sternal manubrium)
Level IVb (Medial Supraclavicular).posterior: Anterior edge of scalene muscles (cranially) / apex of lung, brachiocephalic vessels
Level IVb (Medial Supraclavicular).medial: Common carotid artery / lateral border of level VI
Level IVb (Medial Supraclavicular).drainage: Subglottic larynx, trachea, thyroid, cervical esophagus

Level Va (Upper Posterior Triangle).cranial: Cranial edge of body of hyoid bone

Level Vc (Lateral Supraclavicular).cranial: Transverse cervical vessels plane (caudal border of level V)
Level Vc (Lateral Supraclavicular).caudal: 2 cm cranial to sternal manubrium (caudal border of level IVa)
Level Vc (Lateral Supraclavicular).posterior: Anterior border of trapezius (cranially) / serratus anterior (caudally)

Level VIa (Anterior Jugular).cranial: Caudal edge of hyoid bone or submandibular gland
Level VIa (Anterior Jugular).posterior: Anterior aspect of infrahyoid strap muscles
Level VIa (Anterior Jugular).lateral: Anterior edges of both SCM muscles

Level VIb (Prelaryngeal / Pretracheal /.cranial: Caudal edge of thyroid cartilage (or hyoid for oral tongue/floor of mouth)
Level VIb (Prelaryngeal / Pretracheal /.anterior: Posterior aspect of infrahyoid strap muscles
Level VIb (Prelaryngeal / Pretracheal /.posterior: Anterior aspect of larynx, thyroid gland, trachea; prevertebral muscle (right) / esophagus (left)
Level VIb (Prelaryngeal / Pretracheal /.drainage: Thyroid, glottic/subglottic larynx, piriform sinus apex, cervical esophagus

Level VIIa (Retropharyngeal).cranial: Upper edge of C1 / hard palate
Level VIIa (Retropharyngeal).caudal: Cranial edge of body of hyoid bone
Level VIIa (Retropharyngeal).anterior: Posterior edge of pharyngeal constrictor muscles
Level VIIa (Retropharyngeal).posterior: Longus capitis and longus colli muscles
Level VIIa (Retropharyngeal).lateral: Medial edge of internal carotid artery
Level VIIa (Retropharyngeal).medial: Midline / longus capiti muscle lateral border
Level VIIa (Retropharyngeal).drainage: Nasopharynx, Eustachian tube, soft palate, posterior pharyngeal wall

Level VIIb (Retro-styloid).caudal: Caudal edge of lateral process of C1
Level VIIb (Retro-styloid).anterior: Posterior edge of prestyloid parapharyngeal space
Level VIIb (Retro-styloid).posterior: Vertebral body of C1, base of skull

Level VIII (Parotid Group).boundaries: Zygomatic arch down to mandible, from skin to styloid process, masseter anteriorly to SCM posteriorly
Level VIII (Parotid Group).drainage: Frontal/temporal scalp, eyelids, auricle, parotid gland, nasopharynx

Level IX (Bucco-facial).boundaries: Facial vessels over buccinator muscle, caudal orbit down to mandible
Level IX (Bucco-facial).drainage: Facial skin, nose, buccal mucosa, cheek

Level Xa (Retroauricular / Mastoid).boundaries: Mastoid process, external auditory canal to mastoid tip
Level Xa (Retroauricular / Mastoid).drainage: Posterior ear, external auditory canal, scalp

Level Xb (Occipital).boundaries: Occipital bone protuberance down to upper level Va

entries.title: IASLC / University of Michigan Thoracic Lymph Node Stations CT Atlas
entries.edition_or_version: Chapet et al. 2005 / Rusch et al. 2009

stations.Station 1 (Highest Mediastinal): Above horizontal line at upper rim of brachiocephalic (left innominate) vein where it crosses trachea
stations.Station 2R (Right Upper Paratracheal): Between upper rim of brachiocephalic vein and upper border of aortic arch, to the right of tracheal midline
stations.Station 2L (Left Upper Paratracheal): Between apex of lung/upper rim of manubrium and upper border of aortic arch, to the left of tracheal midline
stations.Station 3A (Prevascular): Anterior to great vessels / superior vena cava, posterior to sternum, from thoracic inlet to carina
stations.Station 3P (Retrotracheal): Posterior to trachea and esophagus, anterior to vertebral body, from thoracic inlet to carina
stations.Station 4R (Right Lower Paratracheal): From cephalic border of aortic arch down to lower border of azygos vein / tracheal bifurcation, to the right of tracheal midline
stations.Station 4L (Left Lower Paratracheal): From upper margin of aortic arch down to upper margin of left main bronchus at level of left upper lobe bronchus carina
stations.Station 5 (Subaortic / AP Window): Subaortic nodes lateral to ligamentum arteriosum, aorta, or left pulmonary artery, proximal to first branch of LPA
stations.Station 6 (Para-aortic): Anterior and lateral to ascending aorta and aortic arch, beneath horizontal line at upper margin of arch
stations.Station 7 (Subcarinal): Caudal to tracheal carina, between right and left main bronchi, down to origin of right middle lobe bronchus / inferior pulmonary veins
stations.Station 8 (Paraesophageal): Nodes lying adjacent to wall of esophagus and to right or left of midline, from carina down to gastroesophageal junction
stations.Station 9 (Pulmonary Ligament): Nodes lying within inferior pulmonary ligament on right (9R) or left (9L), caudal to inferior pulmonary veins
stations.Station 10 (Hilar): Proximal lobar nodes immediately adjacent to mainstem bronchi and pulmonary vessels, distal to mediastinal pleural reflection
stations.Station 11 (Interlobar): Nodes located between the origin of lobar bronchi
stations.Stations 12-14 (Lobar, Segmental, Subseg: Intrapulmonary nodes adjacent to lobar, segmental, and subsegmental bronchi

entries.title: An Atlas of the Pelvic Lymph Node Regions to Aid Radiotherapy Target Volume Definition
entries.edition_or_version: Taylor et al. (2007) / RTOG Consensus Atlas

Common Iliac.caudal: Bifurcation of common iliac vessels into external and internal iliacs (approx. level of sacral promontory)
Common Iliac.vessel_margin: 7 mm expansion around common iliac vessels, extended 10 mm anteriorly over vertebral body, carved off bone and psoas

External Iliac.caudal: Top of femoral head / inguinal ligament (or level of internal obturator vessels)
External Iliac.vessel_margin: 7-8 mm margin around external iliac artery and vein, extended 10+ mm anterolaterally, carved off iliopsoas muscle and pelvic bone

Internal Iliac (Hypogastric).caudal: Level of ischial spine / greater sciatic notch
Internal Iliac (Hypogastric).vessel_margin: 7 mm margin around internal iliac vessels and visceral branches, bounded laterally by pelvic sidewall/obturator internus, medially by ureter/peritoneum

Obturator.cranial: Continuous with external and internal iliac chains
Obturator.boundaries: Runs along medial border of obturator internus muscle and pelvic bone, connecting anterior external iliac with posterior internal iliac nodes

Presacral.boundaries: 10-15 mm pre-vertebral strip anterior to anterior surface of sacrum, bounded anteriorly by posterior rectal wall / mesorectum

Inguino-Femoral.boundaries: Encompasses superficial and deep femoral vessels, sartorius laterally, adductor longus medially, fascia lata anteriorly

Para-Aortic.cranial: Renal vessels / upper border of L2 (or L1 for high risk)
Para-Aortic.boundaries: 8-10 mm margin around aorta and inferior vena cava, connecting to common iliac nodal chains

entries.title: ESTRO / RTOG Consensus Guidelines on Regional Nodal Volume Delineation for Breast Cancer
entries.edition_or_version: Offersen et al. (ESTRO 2015) / RTOG Breast Atlas

Axilla Level I (Low Axilla).boundaries: Lateral to lateral border of pectoralis minor muscle, inferior to axillary vein down to 5th rib / latissimus dorsi
Axilla Level I (Low Axilla).indication: Elective nodal irradiation when axillary dissection omitted or >= 4 positive nodes

Axilla Level II (Mid Axilla).boundaries: Posterior/deep to pectoralis minor muscle, medial to its lateral border and lateral to its medial border
Axilla Level II (Mid Axilla).indication: Included in standard high axillary / supraclavicular field

Axilla Level III (Apical Axilla / Infrac.boundaries: Medial to medial border of pectoralis minor muscle, extending up to caudal margin of clavicle / apex of axilla
Axilla Level III (Apical Axilla / Infrac.indication: Standard component of supraclavicular nodal volume

Level IV / Supraclavicular Nodal Volume.boundaries: Cranial: cricoid cartilage; Caudal: caudal edge of clavicle / junction with level III; Medial: internal jugular vein / SCM; Lateral: junction of clavicle and 1st rib
Level IV / Supraclavicular Nodal Volume.dose: 46-50 Gy in 2 Gy fractions or 40 Gy in 15 fractions

Internal Mammary Nodes (IMN).boundaries: Intercostal spaces 1 to 3 (or 1 to 4) adjacent to internal mammary vessels, anterior to endothoracic fascia/pleura, posterior to ribs/intercostal muscles
Internal Mammary Nodes (IMN).indication: Medial or central tumors, positive axillary nodes, or high-risk features

Interpectoral (Rotter's) Nodes.boundaries: Space between deep surface of pectoralis major and superficial surface of pectoralis minor muscles

entries.title: ICRU Report 83 / AAPM / ASTRO Standardized Target Volume and OAR Nomenclature
entries.organization: International Commission on Radiation Units and Measurements (ICRU)

volume_definitions.GTV (Gross Tumor Volume): Demonstrable extent and location of malignant growth (GTV-P for primary, GTV-N for regional lymph nodes)
volume_definitions.CTV (Clinical Target Volume): Tissue volume that contains GTV and/or subclinical microscopic malignant disease (CTV-P high dose, CTV-N elective nodal volume)
volume_definitions.ITV (Internal Target Volume): Internal margin added to CTV to compensate for internal physiological movements and variation in size, shape, and position (e.g. 4D-CT respiratory motion in lung)
volume_definitions.PTV (Planning Target Volume): Geometrical concept used for treatment planning, adding set-up margin to CTV/ITV to ensure prescribed dose is absorbed in CTV with high probability (usually 95% dose to 95-99% PTV)
volume_definitions.OAR (Organ at Risk): Normal tissue whose radiation sensitivity significantly influences treatment planning and/or prescribed dose
volume_definitions.PRV (Planning Organ at Risk Volume): Margin added around an OAR to account for internal motion and setup variations, critical for serial organs (spinal cord PRV = cord + 1.5-2 mm, brainstem PRV)

expansion_rules.Head & Neck CTV-P: GTV-P + 5 mm anatomically trimmed off bone, cartilage, and air; second intermediate elective margin 5+5 mm for CTV-P2
expansion_rules.Thorax NSCLC CTV: GTV + 5 to 7 mm expansion, edited off uninvolved vertebral body, trachea, and esophagus
expansion_rules.Glioblastoma CTV: GTV (contrast-enhancing cavity + rim on T1+Gd) + 15 to 20 mm expansion, constrained by bony skull, falx, and tentorium
expansion_rules.Prostate PTV Margin: 5 mm radially and 3 mm posteriorly (toward rectum) with daily fiducial/CBCT guidance; 8-10 mm without daily online 3D guidance
